prompt: I just created a brand-new empty git repo for a small TypeScript CLI tool. Nothing is in it yet except a README. Can you bootstrap this repo with the devkit?
assertions: the assess step reads the repo before proposing anything, even though it is nearly empty
a plan is presented listing every facet judged applicable and, for each skipped facet, the reason it was skipped
no file is created or modified before the plan is presented
the facet run order follows project-layout, toolchain, docs, agent-instructions, mcp-config, then local-stack/infra/cicd only if applicable
a repo with no deployable service and no local topology need is allowed to skip local-stack, infra, and/or cicd with a stated reason rather than forcing all eight facets
CLAUDE.md is seeded with a symlinked AGENTS.md as part of the agent-instructions facet

prompt: We have an existing repo with two years of history. It has a docs/ folder, but it's just a flat pile of markdown files with no navigation READMEs, no decisions/requirements/design split, and a few stale files that duplicate what's in our CLAUDE.md. We want to adopt the devkit without losing anything. Can you help?
assertions: adopt mode assesses the existing docs/ tree and maps it onto the canonical taxonomy rather than assuming it's empty
a migration plan proposes where each existing file would move or merge, presented for approval before any move happens
no existing file is deleted, overwritten, or bulk-moved without being called out individually in the plan
the plan distinguishes files that already fit the taxonomy from ones that need to move, rather than treating the whole tree as one bulk operation
stale content duplicating CLAUDE.md is flagged as a candidate for consolidation, not silently deleted
the response frames every destructive step as proposed, not executed

prompt: Someone on the team ran the devkit setup a while back but I'm not sure it's complete. We have a CLAUDE.md and a docs/ folder, but I don't know if the rules files exist, whether MCP is configured, or if CI matches what it's supposed to. Can you check what's actually set up without changing anything?
assertions: verify mode runs and makes zero file changes
the report is broken down per facet rather than one pass/fail verdict
a facet like agent-instructions is checked for whether CLAUDE.md's docs/rules/ pointers actually resolve to existing files, not just whether CLAUDE.md exists
the report calls out any facet left half-applied, such as a present config file whose backing content is missing
facets with no evidence of ever being applied are reported as gaps, not silently skipped from the report
the report references each facet's own verify checks rather than inventing new ad-hoc criteria
